375°F The cut depends on the food, so one number is never the whole answer. Each cell gives the air fryer temperature, °C, gas mark and the share of the oven time you save. Food Basket Oven-style General / mixed 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time Fries & potatoes 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 30% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 25% less time Chicken wings 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time Chicken breast (boneless) 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 25% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time Chicken thighs / bone-in 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time Steak & thick cuts 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time 360°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time Fish & salmon 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time 360°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time Bacon 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 30% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 25% less time Vegetables 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 25% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time Baked goods & cookies 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time 360°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 10% less time Pizza & reheating 350°F / 175°C Gas mark 4 · 25% less time 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 20% less time Casseroles & thick bakes 355°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 15% less time 360°F / 180°C Gas mark 4 · 10% less time What recipes use 375°F 375°F (190°C, gas mark 5) is the working temperature for food that has to brown and cook through at the same pace. Bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks, pork chops, meatballs, sausages, stuffed peppers, puff pastry, hand pies and sheet-pan chicken with vegetables all sit here. It is hot enough for colour without the smoke you get higher up, and it is close to the temperatures air fryer recipes are written at natively, which makes it the easiest setting to convert. A general recipe drops to 350°F. The cut is the same as at lower temperatures, but food reaches the end of the cook in a different state: at this heat a piece of chicken is browned outside well before its centre is done, so the doneness check matters more than the clock. The failure mode at 375°F: brown skin, underdone bone Bone-in chicken is the trap. Skin and the thin end of a drumstick colour quickly in the moving air, so the piece looks ready while the meat against the bone is still pink. Thighs are forgiving because they stay juicy well past 165°F, which is why many cooks take them to 175–185°F; breasts are not, and dry out quickly once they pass 165°F. Arrange pieces skin side up with the thickest part towards the outside of the basket, where the air moves fastest, and turn them once halfway. With pastry the same speed works the other way: the top puffs and browns before the layers underneath have baked. Put pastry on the lowest rack of an oven-style unit, or bake it on a perforated liner so the heat reaches the base. Worked example A recipe roasts bone-in chicken thighs at 375°F for 40 minutes. In a basket air fryer that becomes 350°F (175°C) for 32 minutes; start checking the thickest thigh at 22 minutes and keep going until it reads at least 165°F next to the bone. In an oven-style air fryer, which behaves more like a small convection oven, it is 355°F for 34 minutes. Turn the pieces once at the halfway point in either style. Basket or oven-style at 375°F Here the two styles differ by only a few degrees — 350°F in a basket, 355°F in an oven-style unit — but the time differs more: about 20% less than the oven in a basket and about 15% less in an oven-style unit. A basket moves air faster around a smaller load, so it finishes sooner; an oven-style unit spreads food over racks and cooks more like a fan oven. If yours has two racks, swap them halfway, because the rack nearer the element browns faster. Preheat a basket for 4 minutes; an oven-style unit preheats itself and signals when to add the food. 375°F is 190°C, and the converter accepts either unit. Nearby temperatures 350°F oven to air fryer → 400°F oven to air fryer → Oven to air fryer converter (any temperature) → Printable conversion chart → Frozen food mode (packaging instructions) → Frequently asked questions What is 375°F in an air fryer? Usually 350°F (175°C) in a basket air fryer, with about 20% less time than the oven recipe. An oven-style air fryer needs 355°F. Steak, fish and baked goods are cut less; see the table for each food. What is 375°F in °C, and what do I set on my air fryer? 375°F is 190°C, the figure European recipes and packs usually print. For a basket air fryer set 175°C. If your dial steps in 10°C, round towards the higher setting for chicken and the lower one for pastry. How long do chicken thighs take in the air fryer from a 375°F recipe? Do not set 375°F: set 350°F. Bone-in thighs that take 40 minutes in the oven need about 32 in a basket air fryer. Always confirm with a thermometer — at least 165°F at the bone. Do I need to preheat the air fryer for a 375°F recipe? A short preheat — 4 minutes for a basket, automatic on an oven-style unit — helps pastry rise and skin crisp. For meatballs and stuffed peppers it makes little difference; add a minute to the time instead. Can I cook a whole sheet-pan dinner from a 375°F recipe? Yes, in batches or on two racks of an oven-style unit. Start the chicken first and add the vegetables for the last part of the time, because cut vegetables finish faster than bone-in meat at the same setting.
